scope: Sixth trial: simulator 'step math opcodes not supported' and blank v19 RF frames in the WavEd viewer
console_report: v5 compiled and the .fth stage passed; the simulator reported 'step math opcodes not supported' for both methods and crashed on a second run. Vendor .seq files display in the viewer; v19_research_rf.seq opened with blank waveforms.
rf_viewer_diagnosis: Every vendor RF frame has a non-empty Amplitude expression (formula or user("file.txt")); all six v19 frames had empty expressions on every channel. The stored records followed the vendor real-RF control-word layout exactly.
rf_fix: Each research pulse is now its own single-frame library stored as WavEd stores opt90_as.seq: Amplitude N,user("x.txt");, Frequency NF,0;, and the N-sample text embedded. Rebuilding opt90_as.seq with this encoder and its own expressions reproduces the vendor file byte for byte. Records unchanged (sample_record_sha256 and rfcal numerators identical).
why_one_file_per_pulse: Vendor files only show a one-entry embedded user-file table; the multi-entry layout is undocumented.
compiled_rf_table_check: From the console v5 .fth: v19 frames rf18-rf23 occupy contiguous RF addresses 44928-47968 (unsigned) directly after 19lobe_sinc_2ms, span 2 x records each, RWT=100 equals the file dwell, no overlap.
step_math_assessment: Unresolved. The console is an RTX2000; step instructions implement multiply/divide. The only inline opcodes in the .fth are the compiler's 16-bit multiply (0xB097 0xBE16), which v18 code also uses (vendor tstex check at the top of main). Library math words (D/, D/REM, n/rem, /, */, D*) appear throughout v18-inherited setup and kernel code. No v19-only instruction was identified; running v18 in the simulator is the discriminating test.
ppl_change: Six #use lines (pf18-pf23) replace the combined library; NEWSHAPE_MAC aliases follow. No other line changed.
event_identity_vs_v5: RF timing/frames/multipliers/phases, gradients, ADC and output identical in 6 cases per method
